Narrow the financial-statement representation and clarify payment and closing mechanics without introducing unnecessary complexity in the opening draft.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Please find enclosed the Seller's opening draft for discussion. The draft provides for a USD 45,000,000 purchase price, payable at Closing, and a 30-day closing timetable subject to agreed conditions. We look forward to your comments.

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 45,000,000 for the Shares, payable in full at Closing by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated by the Seller, without set-off or deduction except as required by law.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur within 30 days of signing, subject to satisfaction or waiver by the party entitled to its benefit of the closing conditions expressly set out in this Agreement. The Buyer's obligation to complete the purchase shall not be subject to obtaining financing.

3. Representations. Except as disclosed in the disclosure schedules delivered by the Seller at signing, the Seller represents that the financial statements delivered to the Buyer fairly present, in all material respects, the financial position and results of operations of the Company as of their respective dates and for the periods covered, in accordance with the accounting principles identified in those statements, consistently applied, subject, in the case of unaudited statements, to normal year-end adjustments and the absence of footnotes.

4. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep confidential the terms of this Agreement and the negotiations relating to it, except for disclosures required by applicable law or to its professional advisers, financing sources, and representatives who need to know such information and are bound by confidentiality obligations. No public announcement concerning the transaction shall be made without the other party's prior written consent, except as required by applicable law, in which case the announcing party shall, to the extent legally permitted, consult the other party in advance.

Make a lower counteroffer without claiming unsupported valuation findings, and preserve Buyer's diligence, financing and contractual protections. The supplied metadata appears routine and reveals no apparent confidential negotiating information.

receiver.requested_changes: Counter at USD 35,000,000, subject to satisfactory diligence and agreement on definitive terms. Replace the fixed-price provision with a cash-free, debt-free pricing mechanism, normalized working-capital adjustment and protection against leakage and transaction expenses. Permit agreed escrow, holdback and adjustment deductions. Make Closing conditional on satisfactory diligence, financing, required approvals and consents, accuracy of representations and performance of covenants; use a mutually agreed timetable rather than an unconditional 30-day commitment. Expand Seller representations beyond financial statements, require complete disclosure schedules for review before signing, and add indemnification, appropriate survival periods and escrow security. Include ordinary-course operating covenants, restrictions on distributions and material commitments, and pre-Closing access rights. Retain mutual confidentiality, with express permission to disclose to prospective debt and equity funding sources subject to appropriate confidentiality obligations.

Thank you for the opening draft. The Buyer proposes a purchase price of USD 35,000,000, subject to satisfactory due diligence, agreement on the pricing mechanics and definitive documentation. This is a negotiating proposal, not a binding commitment.

The price should be expressed on a cash-free, debt-free basis with an agreed normalized working-capital target, completion adjustments and appropriate protection against leakage and Seller transaction expenses. The payment provision should accommodate agreed adjustments and an indemnity escrow or holdback.

We cannot accept the current unconditional financing language or commit to Closing within 30 days at this stage. We propose an agreed timetable reflecting diligence, financing, regulatory approvals and third-party consents, with customary conditions covering the accuracy of representations and compliance with pre-Closing covenants.

The draft also requires customary comprehensive Seller representations, disclosure schedules available for review before signing, indemnification and survival provisions, escrow security, ordinary-course covenants and access rights. The confidentiality clause is broadly acceptable, subject to expressly covering prospective debt and equity funding sources under appropriate confidentiality obligations.

Please confirm that the supplied file is your current draft, as its properties contain historical timestamps. We look forward to your response on price and these principal terms.

drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Thank you. The supplied file was our then-current negotiating draft; this revised version supersedes it. Historical file-property timestamps do not indicate an earlier substantive version and are not intended as evidence of execution or agreement.

The Seller counters at USD 40,000,000 on a cash-free, debt-free basis, with a mutually agreed normalized working-capital target and completion adjustments. We have included a proposed 5% indemnity escrow, subject to agreement on the accompanying liability limitations and escrow terms.

We accept a mutually agreed timetable, customary representations and pre-signing disclosure schedules, ordinary-course covenants and reasonable access. Diligence should be completed before signing; we cannot accept an open-ended diligence or financing exit in the definitive agreement. Please identify the Buyer's financing requirements and proposed timetable so that we can address any specific remaining concern.

The revised provisions are negotiating proposals only, subject to contract and agreement on the definitive documentation. Neither party is bound to complete the transaction unless and until definitive agreements are executed.

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price and Adjustments. The proposed enterprise value for the Shares is USD 40,000,000 on a cash-free, debt-free basis, assuming delivery of an agreed normalized level of working capital. The equity purchase price shall equal that enterprise value, plus Company cash, less Company indebtedness and unpaid Seller transaction expenses payable by the Company, and increased or decreased by the amount by which completion working capital exceeds or falls short of the agreed target. Definitions, the target and a sample calculation shall be agreed before signing, using consistent accounting policies and excluding double counting among cash, indebtedness, working capital and transaction expenses. At Closing, the Buyer shall pay the estimated equity purchase price by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the Seller's designated account, less an indemnity escrow equal to 5% of that estimated price deposited with an independent escrow agent under agreed terms. There shall be no other holdback, set-off or deduction except as required by law or expressly agreed. The Buyer shall deliver completion accounts within 60 days after Closing; the Seller shall have 30 days to review and object, with reasonable access to supporting records. Unresolved accounting disputes shall be determined by an independent accountant acting as expert within the scope of the disputed items, and any resulting payment shall be made promptly following final determination. From signing until Closing, no distributions or other transfers of value to the Seller or its affiliates shall be permitted except expressly scheduled permitted payments; any unauthorized transfer shall be reimbursed dollar for dollar to the extent not already reflected in the price adjustment or otherwise recovered. No locked-box leakage recovery shall duplicate completion-account adjustments.

2. Signing and Closing. The parties shall agree a timetable for completion of due diligence, financing arrangements, disclosure schedules and definitive documentation before signing. Closing shall occur on the fifth Business Day following satisfaction or waiver by the entitled party of the agreed closing conditions, or on another mutually agreed date. Conditions shall include required regulatory approvals and specifically identified material third-party consents, absence of any legal prohibition, material compliance with pre-Closing covenants, and accuracy of representations at signing and Closing, subject to agreed materiality standards appropriate to the representations and without duplicative materiality qualifications. There shall be no general satisfactory-diligence or financing condition in the definitive agreement. The Buyer shall provide satisfactory evidence of available funds or binding financing commitments before signing and shall use reasonable best efforts to obtain and maintain its financing. Any proposed exception must be specifically negotiated before signing, including objective conditions, a fixed deadline and appropriate Seller protection. The parties shall cooperate and use reasonable best efforts to obtain required approvals and consents. A mutually agreed outside date and termination provisions shall be included in the definitive agreement.

3. Representations, Disclosure, Covenants and Indemnification. The definitive agreement shall contain customary Seller representations, appropriately qualified by materiality, knowledge where appropriate, and disclosure, concerning capacity and authority, title to the Shares, Company organization and capitalization, financial statements, undisclosed liabilities, taxes, material contracts, litigation, compliance with law, permits, employment and benefits, intellectual property, data protection, material assets and environmental matters. The financial statements representation shall address fair presentation in all material respects under the accounting principles identified in the statements, consistently applied, with customary qualifications for unaudited statements. Complete disclosure schedules shall be provided sufficiently before signing to permit reasonable Buyer review and agreed in connection with signing; no unilateral post-signing disclosure shall cure an existing breach. The Buyer shall provide customary representations concerning authority, enforceability, funds and investment capacity. Between signing and Closing, the Seller shall procure operation of the Company in the ordinary course in all material respects and, except as disclosed, expressly permitted or required by law, no distributions, material commitments outside the ordinary course, material asset disposals or material new indebtedness without the Buyer's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. Reasonable access to relevant records, personnel and premises shall be provided on reasonable notice during business hours, subject to confidentiality, legal privilege, applicable law and non-interference with operations; no contact with employees, customers or suppliers without prior Seller consent. The definitive agreement shall provide reciprocal indemnities for breaches of representations and covenants. Seller liability for general representations shall survive for 18 months, be subject to a deductible basket of 1% of the final equity purchase price and an aggregate cap of 10% of that price. Fundamental representations concerning authority, title and capitalization shall survive for six years and be capped at the final equity purchase price; tax claims shall survive until 60 days after expiry of the applicable statutory limitation period, with tax liability also capped at that price. Covenant claims shall survive for 12 months following the agreed performance date, subject to an aggregate cap equal to that price. Total Seller liability shall not exceed the final equity purchase price, except for the Seller's own fraud, for which no contractual limitation shall apply. Recovery shall exclude duplicative recovery and amounts reflected in the price adjustments, and shall be reduced by insurance proceeds and tax benefits actually realized, net of reasonable recovery costs; the claimant shall reasonably mitigate losses. Indemnification shall be the exclusive monetary remedy after Closing, except for the Seller's own fraud and enforcement of payment and completion-adjustment obligations. The indemnity escrow shall secure Seller claims liabilities under these provisions, shall not increase the applicable caps, and shall be released 18 months after Closing except for amounts reasonably reserved for timely notified, specifically described unresolved claims; reserved amounts shall be released promptly upon resolution. Detailed claims procedures and third-party defense rights shall be agreed.

4. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep confidential the terms of this Agreement, the negotiations relating to it and non-public information received in connection with the transaction, except for disclosures required by applicable law or to its professional advisers, representatives and existing or prospective debt and equity funding sources who need to know such information for the transaction and are subject to appropriate confidentiality obligations. Each party shall be responsible for breaches of those obligations by persons to whom it discloses information. No public announcement concerning the transaction shall be made without the other party's prior written consent, except as required by applicable law, in which case the announcing party shall, to the extent legally permitted, consult the other party in advance. Any existing confidentiality agreement shall remain in force.

receiver.message_back:
Thank you. We acknowledge that the revised draft supersedes the prior negotiating draft and that neither draft constitutes an executed agreement.

On the Buyer’s behalf, we counter at USD 36,000,000 enterprise value on the proposed cash-free, debt-free basis, subject to Buyer approval, satisfactory pre-signing diligence and agreement on definitive documentation. This proposal couples a lower valuation with a path toward execution certainty; it is not an acceptance of the USD 40,000,000 counter.

We can work from your completion-accounts framework, including the prohibition on double counting. Before signing, we must agree the cash, indebtedness, transaction-expense and working-capital definitions, the normalized target, an illustrative calculation and the accounting-policy hierarchy. The expert’s remit should cover accounting disputes, with legal interpretation disputes reserved for the agreed dispute-resolution forum. Any downward adjustment must remain a direct Seller payment obligation, independent of the indemnity escrow.

For indemnification, we propose a 10% escrow, a 0.5% deductible basket, a 15% cap for general representations and 24-month survival, with timely notified claims preserved until resolution. Fundamental and tax protections can proceed broadly on your proposed framework, subject to detailed review. Identified diligence risks will require separately agreed treatment. Any exclusive-remedy provision must preserve equitable relief, enforcement of payment obligations and an appropriate fraud exception, without insulating a party from fraud legally attributable to it. Buyer indemnities should address its own representations and obligations, not automatically mirror the Seller’s risk allocation. Please also replace ‘secure Seller claims liabilities’ with an express statement that the escrow secures the Seller’s indemnification obligations to the Buyer.

We accept completing diligence before signing and can work toward an agreement without a general diligence or financing exit. We cannot yet represent that funds or binding commitments are available: we are confirming the Buyer’s funding structure and any specific requirements and will identify these before signing. No financing-risk allocation is agreed by this letter.

For planning, we propose completing diligence and negotiating documentation within 30 business days after receipt of a substantially complete data room and draft disclosure schedules, subject to timely access and Buyer confirmation. We can accept closing on the fifth business day after satisfaction or waiver of agreed conditions. The outside date should reflect the actual approval and consent requirements.

The expanded representations, pre-signing disclosure process, ordinary-course covenants and confidentiality provisions provide a useful basis for further drafting. All proposals remain subject to contract, Buyer approval and execution of definitive agreements.
